Chapter 141, Section 0138: Definitely Not Neglecting My Proper Work

In the blink of an eye, it was the weekend again, and Chen Guiliang was about to face his makeup exam.

Ao Yanchen used the two days of the weekend to rent a booth at the Talent Building and took Dong Qianqiu to recruit new employees.

In recent days, the criticism of *Wolf Totem* was still brewing.

*Xin Jing* had also entered the fray.

At this time, *Xin Jing* had been established for just over a year. Its sales were up, but its influence was clearly lacking.

It was eager to label itself as "daring to speak the truth" and "speaking up for the people," in order to boost its credibility and authority in the industry.

Its stance was simple: attack whoever was more powerful, attempting to make a name for itself in a single stroke.

Thus, *Xin Jing* began to bombard *Wolf Totem*!

This truly amused Chen Guiliang.

Because the newspaper *Xin Jing* was jointly founded by Guangming Press and Southern Press.

*Guangming* had initially supported *Wolf Totem*, but was now playing dead and staying silent; *Nandu* had been speaking up for *Wolf Totem* all along. And *Xin Jing*, as their illegitimate child, completely ignored what its parents thought, only seeking to seize the opportunity to gain benefits for itself.

To demonstrate its professionalism, *Xin Jing* even produced a comprehensive report, its main selling point being impartiality, objectivity, and fairness.

On the surface, *Xin Jing* seemed to be merely making objective statements.

But there was more. It had actually managed to interview the German sinologist Gu Bin.

Gu Bin said without any mercy: "*Wolf Totem*, to us Germans, is just fascism. This book is a disgrace to China."

Finally, *Xin Jing* also interviewed some educated youth.

It appeared neutral, but in reality, it stripped *Wolf Totem* completely bare.

Once this full-page comprehensive report was published, *Xin Jing* won the goodwill of a large number of intellectuals and ordinary people...

Room 404.

Min Wenyu was lying motionless on his bed.

Chen Guiliang glanced over and asked in a low voice, "What's wrong with Senior Min? At a time like this, shouldn't he be in the library or a study hall?"

Jiang Junlai pulled Chen Guiliang into the hallway. "He's heartbroken."

"He was in a relationship?" Chen Guiliang asked, puzzled.

Jiang Junlai said, "For two of his courses, he chose to take classes at the Guanghua School. Because they often had class together, he fell for a senior from Guanghua. That senior recently got a boyfriend, who is a returnee who came back to China to start a business."

The girl he had a secret crush on got a boyfriend, and he called that being heartbroken?

Chen Guiliang said, "It's good for him to get some rest. He studied way too hard before."

Jiang Junlai began to set himself up for a fall: "I would never have a secret crush on anyone. I'll just work hard to improve my own abilities, and it'll be easy to find a girlfriend in the future. Just like you."

"What's it got to do with me?" Chen Guiliang asked with a smile.

Jiang Junlai said, "In our Yuanpei Class, there are quite a few girls who like you. Do you remember Pan Xiaoyun?"

Chen Guiliang recalled carefully, "She sounds a bit familiar. I think she's in our class."

Jiang Junlai said, "The whole class knows she has a crush on you. When you had your book signing during the winter break, she specially asked a classmate from Beijing to go and queue up to buy your autographed book. She's also playing *Sanguosha*. She bought two physical card sets, one for playing and one for her collection."

"Uh..." Chen Guiliang didn't know what to say.

I guess I'm just too outstanding.

Jiang Junlai smiled. "As long as a man is capable, women will like him. I've already figured this out, so I'm going to study twice as hard! That girl Senior Min has a crush on, the reason she found a returnee for a boyfriend, isn't it because that returnee is more capable?"

"Makes sense," Chen Guiliang nodded.

After chatting for a few more sentences, Chen Guiliang left campus and took a series of transfers to CUEB.

After waiting for a while at the CUEB gate, Bian Guanyue appeared, carrying a guitar on her back, followed by her roommate Lin Ruonan.

Bian Guanyue had a somewhat helpless expression.

"Hi, Chen Guiliang, we meet again," Lin Ruonan waved with a smile.

Chen Guiliang greeted her, "Hello, Lin."

Lin Ruonan complained, "I'm Bian Guanyue's roommate, after all, and I even helped you promote Xiaonei. I sent you a friend request on Xiaonei, why didn't you accept it? I also sent you a message, and you never replied."

"I've been too busy, I didn't notice," Chen Guiliang explained.

Lin Ruonan was quite magnanimous. "Fine, I won't hold it against you. You can at least tell me your QQ number, right?"

Bian Guanyue first looked away, then, worried her boyfriend might be put in a difficult position, said, "Just give it to her, to stop her from saying I'm not a good friend."

Chen Guiliang didn't mind. Giving her his QQ was no big deal.

To him, QQ was now purely work software, used specifically for schmoozing people.

Lin Ruonan saved the QQ number in her phone and waved, "I won't disturb you two lovebirds. Bye!"

"Goodbye, Lin," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

As if forgetting what had just happened, Bian Guanyue pulled Chen Guiliang to lunch first, and then to a nearby hotel to get a room.

After a passionate session, they began to talk about the song.

Bian Guanyue sat cross-legged on the bed, holding her guitar and playing her own song.

Compared to a few days ago, the melody had been slightly altered and was more memorable.

Bian Guanyue asked, "What kind of theme song do you want? I might not be able to write a very good one."

What kind of song?

One that suited the student population, of course.

A song like *Our Memory Book* was more suitable as a high school class anthem, and it had already been released for over a year.

Songs like *The Brightest Star in the Night Sky* and *Dream Chaser's Heart* were high quality and suited students, but they had an excess of positive energy and not enough melancholy.

"I have a melody in my head. I'll sing it, and you can write it down as a score," Chen Guiliang said.

He chose *The Wind Rises*.

He only changed two words in the lyrics, changing "Nagano" to "hometown."

In his past life, he had come across this song countless times on short video apps, but he only remembered the chorus. The first time he saw the full lyrics was when his buddies dragged him to karaoke, where a girl in a JK uniform he was with especially loved to sing it.

The pretty girl in the JK uniform loved to play teacher, leaning against Chen Guiliang's chest and teaching him how to sing the song.

Chen Guiliang thought it was pretty good, but that was all, as he was long past that age.

But as Xiaonei's theme song, it just needed to attract young people!

And it was extremely easy to spread, making it suitable as a promotional song.

"Walking and stopping along this road, following the traces of a drifting youth..."

Chen Guiliang would sing a couple of lines and then pause, giving Bian Guanyue time to notate the score. If she couldn't get it all down, he would sing it again.

In certain parts, he was a little off-key.

Once the main melody was completely written down, Bian Guanyue tried to play and sing it herself.

"This part is wrong."

"But that's how you just sang it."

"Then let's change it again."

"Okay."

For a song she had never heard before, trying to transcribe the score based solely on an a cappella performance was very difficult. Especially since Chen Guiliang was off-key from time to time!

After repeated fumbling, the pitch and rhythm of the main melody were finally determined, but the chords still needed to be worked out slowly.

It was already a feat that Chen Guiliang could sing the lyrics and melody. How would he know anything about chords?

Bian Guanyue wrote out her presumed chords time and again, then played and sang them for Chen Guiliang to hear the effect. Chen Guiliang didn't know how to critique it either, only able to say that a certain part didn't feel right, and then have Bian Guanyue keep revising.

This process was equivalent to Bian Guanyue assisting in the composition, and what's more, she couldn't do it according to her own will. She revised it over and over, but Chen Guiliang was never satisfied.

There were even situations like this—

"Is this okay? We've already revised it seven or eight times."

"I think the first version was the best."

The damn client.

So exhausting!

They kept at it until evening, and Bian Guanyue was already getting a bit agitated. "Why don't we get dinner first? And compose ourselves a little."

"Let's go," Chen Guiliang was also helpless.

He thought just being able to sing it would be enough, but it turned out that was only the main melody, and it needed freaking chords to be a complete composition.

To make matters worse, Bian Guanyue was also a novice and had no experience in this area.

The two had dinner and returned to the hotel to start over.

Fearing he might get frustrated, Bian Guanyue encouraged him, "There's only a little bit left now, we can definitely get it done. You've never learned to write songs, but the lyrics and melody are so good. You're simply a musical genius!"

"This has been hard on you, my standards are a bit too high," Chen Guiliang said. "Actually, many of the chords you came up with were already excellent, they just didn't match what I had in mind. Let's not work on it for now. Come here and kiss me first."

Bian Guanyue immediately threw the guitar aside and, with a blush, got intimate with her boyfriend.

She always acted very shy at the beginning, only truly letting go in the latter half, sometimes becoming particularly wild and willing to try strange positions.

The contrast was quite stark.

Chen Guiliang reveled in it.

After the clouds and rain subsided, the two lay still, holding each other and looking at the lyrics.

Chen Guiliang realized that the composition for *The Wind Rises* didn't have to be exactly the same as the original version; slight differences in detail were normal. As long as the feeling was right.

The same would apply to the arrangement that followed.

In another time and space, the original arrangement of Mai Lajiao's version of *The Wind Rises* was different from the original Japanese version. Later, after it became a hit and capital came in, the Japanese team was invited to re-do the arrangement. As a result, many fans expressed that the high-end Japanese version of the arrangement lacked the flavor of Mai Lajiao's bootleg version.

Chen Guiliang adjusted his thinking. First, he appreciated the lyrics with Bian Guanyue, and then slowly found the right feeling based on the lyrics.

This time, it went much more smoothly.

The final version they came up with had a main melody consistent with the original song, while the chords had extremely subtle differences.

On Sunday, Chen Guiliang returned to Peking University and treated Senior Kong to barbecue—the same senior who did the Dongbei accent for Sun Quan.

"How much does it cost to hire someone for a song arrangement these days?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chewing on a grilled kidney, Senior Kong said, "Depends on your budget. For those famous pop stars, the arrangement is often done by a top professional leading a whole team. The price is ridiculously high. And hiring someone from Hong Kong or Taiwan for an arrangement is much more expensive than hiring someone from the mainland."

Chen Guiliang said, "My budget is within 8,000 yuan."

"That's doable. That budget is more than enough," Senior Kong asked, "What style are you looking for?"

Chen Guiliang didn't know anything about styles, so he simply took out the lyrics and music for *The Wind Rises*.

There was no need to worry about plagiarism. If Senior Kong dared to plagiarize it, he could forget about surviving at Peking University, and would even have a hard time in the music circle in the future.

Senior Kong hummed the song twice while looking at the score and said in surprise, "You wrote this yourselves? That's pretty amazing!"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang said shamelessly.

Music: Chen Guiliang, Bian Guanyue. Lyrics: Chen Guiliang.

The stage name "Li Jing," which Bian Guanyue had picked for herself, had been mercilessly vetoed by Chen Guiliang.

Senior Kong studied the lyrics and music repeatedly and said, "There's a guy named Peng Fei. His price and style are very suitable. This guy is from Dongbei, just like me. He graduated from the Shanghai Conservatory of Music less than two years ago and is now active in Beijing's jazz and indie music scenes. He did the string section for Li Jian's song *Legend*."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How much does he charge?"

Senior Kong said, "Between 5,000 and 8,000, but you'll have to negotiate the specific price with him. He's eager to make a name for himself, and your song is good, so you'll probably be able to get the price down to the minimum."

"Thanks, Senior Kong!"

Was Chen Guiliang neglecting his proper work by spending so much effort on a song?

This was part of his job as Xiaonei's product manager. *The Wind Rises* could become a powerful tool for promoting Xiaonei!

(End of this chapter)
